claims.statement: All Open-Inspect services emit structured logging as flat single-line JSON carrying a shared envelope — level, service, component, msg (the stable event identifier used for filtering), and ts (epoch ms) — produced in TypeScript services by the zero-dependency createLogger factory in packages/shared/src/logger.ts.

Logger-owned keys (level, component, msg, ts, service) cannot be spoofed: RESERVED_KEYS are stripped from base context and per-call data, while other structured fields merge base context → child context → per-call data with later values overriding earlier ones, and logger.child() forks context without mutating the parent logger.

An Error passed as data.error is normalized into the shared error fields error_type (class name), error_message, error_stack, and error_code (when the error carries a string code) — the error reporting convention used across all services.

Logging can never crash a request: JSON.stringify is wrapped so a serialization failure (circular structures, bigints) degrades to a guaranteed-serializable LOG_SERIALIZE_FAILURE line carrying the original message and level.

Severity is emitted with real console semantics (debug/info → console.log, warn → console.warn, error → console.error) while the JSON level field drives programmatic filtering; lines below the configured minimum level are dropped, and parseLogLevel resolves the LOG_LEVEL env var against an explicit allowlist, defaulting to info.

Each package wraps the shared factory and pre-binds its service name so call sites only choose a component: control-plane ("control-plane"), slack-bot, linear-bot, github-bot, and web ("web", which also parses LOG_LEVEL from the Node process env).

The Python sandbox runtime and modal-infra share the same log envelope through JSONFormatter/StructuredLogger in sandbox_runtime.log_config.py (service fixed to "modal-infra", exceptions exploded to error_type/error_message/truncated error_stack, third-party library logs included), with one naming nuance: the Python formatter emits the stable event identifier under the `event` key, whereas the TypeScript envelope uses `msg` (with much control-plane code repeating it under `event`).

The correlation fields are trace_id (cross-service, generated at the router/bot edge), request_id (single HTTP hop, router), session_id (session lifetime, control plane on create), message_id (single prompt run, control plane on enqueue), sandbox_id (sandbox lifetime, sandbox backend on create/restore), and opencode_session_id (OpenCode process, supervisor on ensure) — call sites include whichever are available.

Correlation naming is canonical at every transport boundary per ADR 0002: snake_case keys (trace_id, request_id, session_id, sandbox_id), HTTP headers x-trace-id/x-request-id/x-session-id/x-sandbox-id, provider/client correlation objects with the same keys, and a single boundary conversion for camelCase modules so traceId/trace_id are never mixed within one boundary.

The control-plane router builds the per-request RequestContext with trace_id taken from the inbound x-trace-id header or a fresh crypto.randomUUID() and an 8-character request_id, and echoes both in x-request-id/x-trace-id on every response including the CORS preflight, so callers can correlate against the control plane even when they sent no trace.

The web (Next.js) middleware stamps /api/:path* with a grammar-validated inbound x-trace-id (or a generated UUID) plus a fresh hop-local request id, and forwards only x-trace-id to the control plane via buildServiceAuthHeaders; the control plane still mints its own per-hop request_id.

The Slack bot mints trace_id at its edge (crypto.randomUUID() on POST /events) and accepts an inbound x-trace-id on its callback routes (the trace echoed back by the control plane), passing the trace through signed control-plane calls and repeating it in its own control_plane.create_session / control_plane.send_prompt / callback.complete logs.

Control-plane → Session Durable Object calls propagate correlation via x-trace-id/x-request-id headers; the DO's SessionHttpDispatcher binds them into a per-request child logger without mutating the shared session logger (preventing trace leakage across interleaved requests and later callbacks), falling back to the session logger when headers are absent — an invariant guarded by an integration test with overlapping distinct-trace requests.

The session-scoped logger injects the current public session_id at emit time through a latched resolver: it logs the Durable Object id until /internal/init writes the session row, then upgrades to the public id automatically for every component in the graph, while explicit per-call data can still override it.

Sandbox provider clients accept a CorrelationContext and convert it at the transport boundary: ModalClient sets x-trace-id, x-request-id, x-session-id, and x-sandbox-id headers; the Vercel client sets x-trace-id/x-request-id and repeats the values in its vercel_sandbox.request logs.

Each service logs one wide event per unit of work: http.request (router, one per HTTP request, with D1 aggregates spread in from ctx.metrics.summarize()), do.request (session DO dispatcher, with duration_ms/handler_ms/outcome; WebSocket upgrades and unmatched routes excluded), and modal.http_request (modal-infra's _execute_endpoint wrapper, reading correlation from the x-trace-id/x-request-id/x-session-id/x-sandbox-id headers).

Wide events carry an `outcome` field with a shared vocabulary of success, error, rejected (denied before processing — auth/validation), timeout, and cancelled, extended per event: prompt.enqueue reports enqueued/deduplicated/conflict/rejected(queue_full), prompt.dispatch reports deferred/sent/send_failed, and ws.connect reports success/auth_failed/rejected/auth_timeout with a reject_reason (sandbox_id_mismatch, token_mismatch, session_terminal, sandbox_stopped, …).

The router's http.request wide event maps outcome to success/error by HTTP status (≥ 500 is error); a handler throwing a non-HttpError logs the error variant with the error field and returns a generic 500.

Fire-and-forget background work is observable: the Cloudflare BackgroundTasks adapter logs background_task.failed with the task name and its correlation context whenever a waitUntil task throws, so callbacks, snapshotting, and queue processing never fail silently.

D1 instrumentation: instrumentD1 wraps the SqlDatabase port so every terminal statement call (run/first/all, with bind() re-wrapping for chaining) records a D1QueryRecord — wall-clock query_ms plus engine-reported d1_server_ms/rows_read/rows_written — into a per-request RequestMetrics; batch() unwraps wrapped statements via the ORIGINAL_STMT symbol (the same-origin contract) and records one aggregate record; summarize() folds everything into d1_query_count, d1_total_ms, d1_server_total_ms, d1_rows_read, d1_rows_written, plus one <name>_ms field per named metrics.time span.

Routes use metrics.time() to time non-D1 work as named spans (e.g. kv_read for the repos cache, scm_api for SCM API calls, do_fetch for internal Durable Object fetches), which surface as <name>_ms fields in the wide event.

The instrumented handle is injected as ctx.db and stores take the SqlDatabase port unchanged; an ESLint no-restricted-syntax rule bans .DB access under packages/control-plane/src outside tests, exempting only the composition roots (router.ts and the Durable Object constructors); the WebSocket upgrade path in index.ts builds its own instrumented handle so upgrade-time reads are timed too; and the observability metadata in SqlResult.meta is optional and never load-bearing (meta.changes is the only correctness-gating field).

AnalyticsStore serves session analytics over the sessions table, filtered by default to HUMAN_SPAWN_SOURCES (user, slack-bot, linear-bot, github-bot) so automation sessions are excluded: getSummary returns totals, distinct active users via COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(user_id, NULLIF(scm_login, ''))) with a documented Phase 4→6 rollout window that can temporarily double-count a person, total/average cost, PRs, and a status breakdown; getTimeseries buckets per day per user identity; getBreakdown groups by user or repo (null repo keys render as "No repository").

PullRequestAnalyticsStore implements PR value-stream analytics over session_pull_requests with a deliberately different contract from session analytics: the universe is pull requests with no spawn-source filter (automation-produced PRs are output, surfaced via the source dimension), all reads execute in one D1 batch so every metric in a response shares one snapshot even under concurrent lifecycle webhooks, three different populations are used (created-in-window cohort for funnel/repos/sources, merged-in-window for merge latency, windowless open inventory anchored at filters.now), and PR creation time is COALESCE(provider_created_at, created_at).

The analytics routes expose GET /analytics/summary, /analytics/timeseries, /analytics/breakdown?by=user|repo, and /analytics/pull-requests under the SCM-agnostic user-or-service policy; the days parameter is validated against the shared allowlist ANALYTICS_DAYS = [7, 14, 30, 90] (default 30, anything else a 400 listing valid values), and the PR filters add a now anchor for the open-inventory age computation.

Terraform's shared cloudflare-worker module enables Cloudflare Workers Observability on deployed workers with head_sampling_rate = 1 and invocation logs, so every console JSON line becomes queryable telemetry.

scripts/cf-logs.ts queries the Cloudflare Workers Observability Telemetry Query API to fetch historical control-plane logs by --session (matching the application session_id field), --request-id ($metadata.requestId: app-level request_id on fetch events, the Cloudflare platform id on Durable Object events), --trace ($metadata.traceId), --search (substring on $metadata.message), --level, or --script/--all; application fields live under `source` in each event, not at the top level; it requires CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (Workers:Read) and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, supports --mins lookback (default 30, max 7 days), --limit (default 1000), and --json output for piping to an LLM.

modal-infra runs as a Modal App with FastAPI endpoints rather than a Cloudflare Worker, so its JSON logs are captured by the Modal platform instead of Workers telemetry; cross-service joins to it use trace_id/sandbox_id, which its endpoints read from the correlation headers into the modal.http_request wide event.

docs/DEBUGGING_PLAYBOOK.md is the operator-facing per-service event catalog and scenario reference (control-plane router/image-builds/session-do/lifecycle-manager/provider clients, modal-infra api/sandbox/supervisor/bridge, slack-bot handler/attachments/callback/completion-media and more); dashboards must use the outcome-bearing sandbox.spawn/sandbox.restore event names (the legacy sandbox.spawned, sandbox.spawn_failed, and sandbox.restored names are superseded).

Redaction and level rules apply to all services: never log authorization headers, HMAC tokens derived from MODAL_API_SECRET, sig1 service signatures, GitHub App private keys or installation tokens, GitHub OAuth tokens, or sandbox auth tokens; body content stays out of logs unless explicitly whitelisted and truncated; LOG_LEVEL defaults to info per service (debug for staging, info or warn for production).

A Slack prompt run joins across services by trace_id at the HTTP hops and by message_id within a run: slack-bot http.request → control_plane.create_session/send_prompt, control-plane http.request and prompt.enqueue (assigning message_id) → prompt.dispatch, modal-infra modal.http_request and sandbox.create/restore, the DO settling the run with prompt.complete (total/processing/queue duration) and the delivery chain callback.complete_delivery → callback.complete; DO-internal work outside any request (alarms, background tasks) has no request correlation, so session_id is the join key there.
